results.name: double_or_half_of_example_yes
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets equal to twice or half of a shown example; observed above null means people use multiplicative (doubling/halving) relations more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: double_or_half_of_example_yes
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets equal to twice or half of a shown example; observed above null means people use multiplicative (doubling/halving) relations more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    m = (x.mul(2).eq(t, axis=0) | x.div(2).eq(t, axis=0)).any(axis=1) & ~isin
    v = r[m].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: per_set_yes_rate_sd
results.description: Standard deviation across number_sets of the per-set yes rate; observed above null means sets differ in generalization breadth more (model too uniform across sets), below means the model exaggerates set-to-set differences.

    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)

results.name: digit_reversal_target_yes
results.description: Yes rate for non-example two-digit targets that are the digit reversal of a shown example (e.g. 38 for 83); observed above null means people generalize by digit reversal more than the model (which has no reversal concept) predicts.
results.code:
# name: digit_reversal_target_yes
# description: Yes rate for non-example two-digit targets that are the digit reversal of a shown example (e.g. 38 for 83); observed above null means people generalize by digit reversal more than the model (which has no reversal concept) predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    rev = (t % 10) * 10 + t // 10

    v = r[m].mean()
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: decade_boundary_near_extrapolation
results.description: For 1-2 example sets, among non-example targets outside the span within 6 of the nearest example, yes rate when the target shares that example tens digit minus when it crosses into another decade; observed above null means decade boundaries limit generalization more than the decade-blind model predicts.
results.code:
# name: decade_boundary_near_extrapolation
# description: For 1-2 example sets, among non-example targets outside the span within 6 of the nearest example, yes rate when the target shares that example tens digit minus when it crosses into another decade; observed above null means decade boundaries limit generalization more than the decade-blind model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    d2 = dist.fillna(999).values
    near = x.values[np.arange(len(x)), d2.argmin(axis=1)]
    m = ((n <= 2) & ~isin & (nd <= 6) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx))).values
    sd = (t.values // 10) == (near // 10)
    a = r.values[m & sd].mean() if (m & sd).any() else np.nan
    b = r.values[m & ~sd].mean() if (m & ~sd).any() else np.nan
    v = a - b
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: ap_lattice_minus_offlattice_yes
results.description: Among sets whose sorted examples are evenly spaced with step >= 3, yes rate for non-example targets within two steps of the span lying on the progression lattice minus those off it; observed above null means people extrapolate arithmetic progressions more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: ap_lattice_minus_offlattice_yes
# description: Among sets whose sorted examples are evenly spaced with step >= 3, yes rate for non-example targets within two steps of the span lying on the progression lattice minus those off it; observed above null means people extrapolate arithmetic progressions more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    s = np.sort(x.values, axis=1)
    dif = np.diff(s, axis=1)
    with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
        step = np.where(n.values >= 2, np.nanmin(np.where(np.isnan(dif), np.inf, dif), axis=1), 0.0)
        big = np.where(n.values >= 2, np.nanmax(np.where(np.isnan(dif), -np.inf, dif), axis=1), -1.0)
    ap = (n.values >= 2) & (big == step) & (step >= 3)
    st = np.where(ap, step, 1.0)
    lat = ((t.values - mn.values) % st) == 0
    w = ap & ~isin.values & (t.values >= mn.values - 2 * st) & (t.values <= mx.values + 2 * st)
    a = r.values[w & lat].mean() if (w & lat).any() else np.nan
    b = r.values[w & ~lat].mean() if (w & ~lat).any() else np.nan
    v = a - b
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)

results.name: interior_near_minus_far_4ex
results.description: For 4-example sets, among non-example targets strictly inside the example span, yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus targets >= 10 from every example; observed above null means people show an exemplar-like similarity gradient inside the span that the range model flattens, below means interior gaps are filled more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: interior_near_minus_far_4ex
# description: For 4-example sets, among non-example targets strictly inside the example span, yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus targets >= 10 from every example; observed above null means people show an exemplar-like similarity gradient inside the span that the range model flattens, below means interior gaps are filled more than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    dist = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs()
    nd = dist.min(axis=1)
    m = (n == 4) & ~isin & (t > mn) & (t < mx)
    a = r[m & (nd <= 3)].mean()
    b = r[m & (nd >= 10)].mean()
    v = a - b
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or np.isnan(v)) else v)
